h1: Opening a craft beer bottle shop in India
title: Opening a Craft Beer Bottle Shop | Craft Beer School
desc: A practical guide to opening a craft beer bottle shop in India: the licence route, stock and fridge planning, supplier terms and pricing to protect margin.
teaser: Selling beer in bottles looks simple. Then the fridge, the licence and the dating on the label arrive.
standfirst: A bottle shop has no kitchen, no brewhouse and no table service. What it has is a fridge, a licence and a shelf of products that go stale. Here is what to settle before you take a lease.
sections: Why a bottle shop is harder than it looks

Retail seems the gentle end of the beer business. No chefs, no brewers, no tap lines. The catch is that you hold a perishable product on shelves, usually in a hot country. Customers cannot taste it before they buy.

You also depend on a licence category that is tightly controlled. In India alcohol is a state subject, so who may sell packaged beer, from what kind of premises and at what retail price differ between states and change through notifications. Many states restrict retail to a limited number of licensed shops. Speak to a licensing consultant about the current position before you spend on a site.
Pick the shop type your state allows

States define retail in different ways. Some allow standalone shops. Some allow sale within a larger store. Some limit sale to hotels, restaurants or authorised outlets. Some allow takeaway from a brewpub. Our guide on craft beer rules by state shows how widely the rules vary. Treat it as a starting point, not a final answer.

The shop type then decides location, size, opening hours and who your neighbours can be. Schools, places of worship and certain zones may be off limits. Check the distance rules in your state before you shortlist sites.
Plan the fridge before the shelves

Beer is best held cold. A pasteurised mainstream lager tolerates room temperature far better than unpasteurised craft beer, but hoppy beers lose aroma quickly when warm. For your hoppiest products, aim to keep them refrigerated at about 2 to 4 °C from the delivery to the sale.

That has a cost. A walk-in cold room costs far more than a wall of glass-door fridges, but it holds more stock cold and keeps it steadier than fridges that are opened all day. Measure the shop's power supply and the heat load before you order. Our guide on fridge rotation in a bottle shop covers the day to day routine: first in, first out and a weekly check of dates.

New shop owners tend to stock everything. The better route is a tight range by style and price, topped up weekly. Keep a few steady sellers that bring people in. Add a rotating shelf of seasonal and limited beers.

Look at the best before date every time a delivery arrives. Ask suppliers for the packaging date if it is not on the label. Reject stock that is already well into its life. Craft cans and bottles from small breweries commonly carry a shorter shelf life than mainstream packaged beer, so ordering smaller quantities more often usually beats a big buy.

Ask every supplier the same questions. What is the minimum order? How often can they deliver? Who bears the loss on beer that is damaged or expires? Can slow lines be returned or swapped? Is the retail price fixed by the state, or can you set it within limits?

Pricing rules differ by state. Some fix the maximum retail price. Some allow shops to set their own. Know your position before you build a margin plan. Our guide on craft beer market trends in India helps you think about what a local customer will pay.
Run the numbers on dead stock

A bottle shop earns a small margin on each sale, so losses from expired stock matter. Here is an illustration with round, made up figures. If a shop earns ₹40 gross on a bottle, then writing off one case of 24 bottles that cost ₹150 each wipes out the gross margin on 90 other bottles (₹3,600 of cost divided by ₹40).

Track weekly sales by line and stop reordering anything that sits. Keep as little of your cash as you can on shelves where it ages.

You are selling an age restricted product. Check identification, refuse sale to anyone underage or visibly intoxicated and follow your state's rules on hours and display. Many shops add a responsible drinking notice at the counter.

Before you commit to a site, write down the licence route, the fridge capacity, your supplier terms and a monthly cash flow. Brewery Business Management teaches that modelling for beverage retail and production alike.
faqs: Can anyone open a craft beer bottle shop in India?
No. Alcohol retail is licensed by each state and the number and type of shops are often limited. Check the current rules or consult a licensing adviser.
Do craft beers need to be refrigerated in a shop?
Hoppy and unpasteurised beers keep best at about 2 to 4 °C. Mainstream pasteurised beer tolerates warmth better, but cold storage still protects quality.
How much stock should a new bottle shop hold?
Start small and reorder often. Craft beer has a limited shelf life, so a big opening order risks expired stock.
Why does best before date matter so much?
Beer fades with age and heat. Hop aroma drops and stale flavours appear. Customers blame the shop as much as the brewery.
